items.wrong: If I will be patient, I would listen.
items.fix: If I were patient, I would listen.
items.why: Depois de if, use o passado, não will nem would.

items.wrong: If I am you, I will call.
items.fix: If I were you, I would call.
items.why: Para conselho, use If I were you + would.

items.wrong: If I had more confidence, I wouldn’t to worry.
items.fix: If I had more confidence, I wouldn’t worry.
items.why: Depois de would use o verbo sem to.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: If I will be patient, I would listen. → If I were patient, I would listen. | If I am you, I will call. → If I were you, I would call. | If I had more confidence, I wouldn’t to worry. → If I had more confidence, I wouldn’t worry..
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.big: If I were more patient, I would listen better
facts.label: Segundo condicional
facts.sub: Use If + passado, would + verbo para situações imaginárias. Para conselho: If I were you, I would….

facts.label: se eu fosse
facts.sub: Use If I were para imaginar uma qualidade que você não tem agora: If I were more patient. Com I, he e she, em conselhos use were.

facts.label: eu faria
facts.sub: Depois da condição use would + verbo sem to: I would listen better. A forma curta é I’d: I’d listen better.

mini.en: I lost my temper with a client. If I were more patient, I would {listen better|work harder|sleep more}.
mini.pt: Perdi a paciência com um cliente. Se eu fosse mais paciente, {escutaria melhor|trabalharia mais|dormiria mais}.

compare.ask: If I were more patient, I would listen better.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “se eu fosse mais paciente, escutaria melhor”.
compare.tip: Diga: “if I were more patient, I would listen better.”
compare.us: Em inglês, use If + passado + would + verbo: If I were more patient, I would listen better. Com be, use were para todas as pessoas. Para conselho, use If I were you, I would….

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: If I were more patient, I would listen better.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: If I were more patient is not real now.
items.why: Yes, it is imaginary.

items.s: We say “If I was you” only in formal English.
items.why: If I were you is the usual advice form, but was is also used in speech.

items.s: After would we use the base verb.
items.why: Yes.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: If I were more patient is not real now. → Verdadeiro (Yes, it is imaginary.)
We say “If I was you” only in formal English. → Falso (If I were you is the usual advice form, but was is also used in speec…)
After would we use the base verb. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 2/2

items.s: We say “If I would be patient”.
items.why: We say If I were patient.

items.s: We use the second conditional to give advice with If I were you.
items.why: Yes.

pages.instruction: Mais uma rodada: decida e explique.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We say “If I would be patient”. → Falso (We say If I were patient.)
We use the second conditional to give advice with If I were you. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A home in Leeds · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a quiet Tuesday evening in Leeds. Fay opens the door and sees her friend Leo. His face looks tired and sad. She makes tea and brings two cups. Leo sits on the sofa with a long sigh. He starts to explain his bad day.

“Leo, you look upset. What happened at work today?” says Fay. “I lost my temper with a client. If I were more patient, I would listen better.” says Leo. “If I were you, I would call the client and say sorry.” says Fay.
